what_happened: render_next()'s existing terminal-member-omission convention and build_ready_pool()'s readiness predicate together gave an exact, reusable precedent for the roadmap-aware candidate filter -- no new readiness logic had to be designed, and a live jq simulation against the current state.json confirmed the proposed walk-and-filter rule behaves sensibly (4 leading batches skip at zero probe cost, 5th batch's singleton [577] is the first live candidate).

Research report 01 pre-settled the design decision (Direction (a)) with live-corpus validation and an enumerated test list, so plan authoring needed only sizing/sequencing plus two new mechanical findings (usage() sed-range coupling at orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh:99 and the index-entries.json line_count coupling for the template edit); no re-derivation of the diagnosis was needed.

Plan phases 1-4 edit the source store (agent-system/extensions/core/**) with redeploy deferred to Phase 5, but this suite's default CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE resolution is deploy-tree-first: it silently resolves and copies the STALE deployed .claude/scripts/orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh into build_scratch() rather than the edited source-store copy, unless CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store is exported. Phase 1 and Phase 2's own run-all.sh --only invocations (run without that override) therefore validated the pre-edit deployed script, not the edits -- a false-confidence result that happened not to produce a false PASS only because the pre-existing cases are genuinely unchanged by the refactor. Re-ran both phases' verification with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store exported and confirmed all cases, including the new Phase 3 roadmap-walk cases, pass against the actual edited script.

Phase 3's Scope Hypothesis declared the test file alone, but writing the new roadmap-walk regression cases surfaced a real bug in Phase 2's own implementation: mode_next_batch() populated READY_SET by calling build_ready_set() (via build_ready_pool()) inside a process-substitution subshell (done < <(build_ready_pool)), so the associative array never persisted back to the parent shell where task_is_ready() is later called from suggest_from_roadmap_batches() -- every batch was therefore seen as empty-filtered regardless of real readiness. Fixed by calling build_ready_set() directly in mode_next_batch()'s own shell before building the ready array. Also added a visible 'Authored roadmap batch N: skipped' line for an empty-filtered batch (Phase 2's own text only recorded the skip in a counter, not visibly, which could not satisfy the new case (o) acceptance -- 'first batch's skip is visible in the output'). Both fixes landed in orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh during Phase 3, a declared excursion beyond that phase's test-file-only Scope Hypothesis, recorded here rather than silently absorbed.

Plan Phase 4's Decision states Rule R (index-entries.json line_count accuracy) is 'advisory here (no pre-commit hook installed)'. Verified live: that framing is correct for GIT COMMITS (no pre-commit hook invokes check-extension-docs.sh, so a plain git commit is never blocked), but check-extension-docs.sh's own INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE defaults to 'hard', not advisory -- a direct invocation of the script (or verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4, Phase 4's own covering check) genuinely exits 1 on the declared line_count drift unless INDEX_TRUTH_GATE_MODE=advisory is exported. Confirmed with that override that the ONLY remaining core-extension failures are the two expected items: the declared line_count drift (both files this phase edited) and 'deployed script content drift' for the two files Phase 2/3 edited in the source store (expected until Phase 5's redeploy makes the deployed and source trees identical again). No other doc-lint or task-reference finding exists. Phase 4 closes on this evidence rather than a literal zero-exit verify-deploy.sh run, consistent with the plan's own Decision 4 and Phase 5's stated reconciliation role.

Phase 5's live --next-batch attestation against this repository's real specs/state.json (152 active_projects) crashed silently: exit 1, zero stdout/stderr, no documented exit code (script documents only 0/2/3). Root cause: build_ready_set()'s 'if [ "$all_ok" = true ] && READY_SET[...]=1' (inherited verbatim from the pre-refactor build_ready_pool() one-liner, per Phase 1's move-don't-restate instruction) is the classic set -e footgun -- when the && list's left side is false, the whole statement's nonzero exit status propagates and aborts the script, UNLESS that statement runs inside a process-substitution subshell (the pre-refactor call site), where the subshell's death is insulated from the parent. The live state.json's highest-numbered active task (644) is not_started with an unmet dependency (all_ok=false), and it sorts last in build_ready_set()'s scan order -- exactly the triggering position. This bug was LATENT in the original script (same shape, same risk) but never manifested because Mode A's only call site ran it inside <(build_ready_pool), accidentally insulating the crash; Phase 2's fix for the READY_SET-persistence bug (calling build_ready_set() directly in mode_next_batch()'s own shell, required so task_is_ready() can see it) removed that accidental insulation and exposed it. Fixed by converting the bare && list to an explicit if/then. Added regression case (s) to the suite, confirmed to genuinely fail against the unfixed code (exit 1, zero output) and pass with the fix. Re-verified all 27 cases green, then redeployed and re-ran the live attestation, which now succeeds.

Phase 5 declares no Scope Hypothesis (its Files to modify are __WHOLE_TREE__ and index-entries.json), but discovering the set -e footgun crash during its own live-attestation task (a required Phase 5 task) justified adding one new regression case (case s) to test-orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh and the matching fix to orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh -- both source-store files Phase 2/3 already own. Recorded explicitly rather than silently absorbed, same class as the Phase 3 scope excursion.
